alpha_multiple_testing.family: the nine intercept tests formed by three fixed assets times three fixed models
alpha_multiple_testing.method: Holm step-down adjusted p-values, reported alongside nominal HAC p-values
alpha_multiple_testing.selection_warning: These intervals and p-values remain approximate and model-conditional; the nine fitted specifications do not represent every possible model a researcher could try.

model_comparison_limitations: FF3 and FF5 use different official SMB constructions (size/book-to-market versus the average of size/book-to-market, size/profitability and size/investment spreads); the monthly differences have not been rebuilt from underlying portfolios. The specific reason for the Mkt-RF file differences remains unverified.
Because their common-name factor realizations differ, FF3 and FF5 are not treated as strictly nested for an F-test.
The R-squared difference is not attributed solely to adding RMW and CMA.

chronological_attribution_check.purpose: fixed time-order descriptive coefficient stability and same-month attribution error
limitations: The snapshot is not point-in-time; historical inputs may have been revised after each month.
Evaluation-period factor returns are realized within the evaluated months and are only known after month-end, so this is not a real-time forecast, signal evaluation, or strategy test.
No costs, financing, borrow, trade, or net return are calculated.

costs_and_execution.transaction_costs: not applicable: no signal, order, turnover, or trade ledger
costs_and_execution.financing_and_borrow: not applicable: no positions or financing/borrow ledger

interpretation_limitations: Regression coefficients are conditional historical associations, not causal effects.
Alpha is the fitted intercept relative to the chosen factors and sample; it changes with model specification and is not proof of mispricing, skill, or future performance.

HAC standard errors and t-based intervals use a declared Bartlett bandwidth and finite-sample correction; the computation does not verify assumptions or guarantee reliable inference in this finite sample.
An in-sample fitted-versus-residual variance identity is an OLS accounting result, not evidence that future residuals are independent or predictable.
Correlated factors prevent assigning each factor an independent additive share of explained variance from these marginal betas alone.
Nominal tests and confidence intervals are exploratory; the nine-alpha Holm adjustment addresses that displayed family but not unreported model search or specification choice.
